## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vohārakathā* ("Points of Controversy on Utterance" or "Speech") is the tenth discourse in the second chapter (*vagga*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Theravāda *Abhidhamma Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. The debate centers on the utterance (*vohāra*) of the Buddha, addressing whether all persons who hear the Buddha's utterance immediately develop or bring into being the path (*magga*) [Skorupski 1991]. This discussion belongs to a broader doctrinal controversy regarding whether the speech of the Buddha is transcendent or supramundane (*lokuttara*), and it intersects with the Abhidhamma problem of momentariness—specifically whether multiple mental phenomena occur concurrently or in rapid sequential order [Skorupski 1991]. SuttaCentral records one translation of the text [SuttaCentral].
